text:
Mikko Rantanen has 22 points in 20 games for Dallas, 10 of them on the power play, and on the surface his second full season with the Stars looks like his usual production. Look closer at the goals. He has nine on just 37 shots, shooting 24% against 16% last season, on 5.7 expected goals. That's the kind of rate that rarely lasts, and it's covering for a quieter shooting season than his history (0.86 expected goals per 60 against 1.02 last year).

His ice time has also slipped, down 1:49 a night over his last ten games to 19:00, with nine points in that stretch, a little under what we'd expect. The five-on-five game is fine: Dallas takes 56.1% of the expected goals with him on the ice, six points better than without him.

What to watch is volume. He went without a shot against New Jersey and Winnipeg. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries last season, and his top speed of 23.5 mph sits in the 98th percentile. The legs are there. The shots have to come back for the goals to keep coming.
headline: Rantanen is scoring on very few shots
